title: High-resolution angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy with tunable magnetic field
authors: Jairo Obando-Guevara, Huu-Thong Le, Emiliano Corcino Aracena, Sayan Singha, Kyungchan Lee, Yingdong Guan, Zhiqiang Mao, Dezhe Jin, Chaoxing Liu, Heike Pfau
abstract: The control and perturbation of quantum phenomena with magnetic fields is an indispensable tool in materials research. Recently, in-situ field tuning was implemented into angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (magneto-ARPES), which provides direct momentum and energy-resolved information of the field-dependent electronic structure. However, aberrations of the electron trajectories were shown to be substantial, leading to significant spectral distortions and broadening even in small fields. Here we show that the electronic structure can be recovered from magneto-ARPES spectra with high accuracy while maintaining high momentum resolution even when strong trajectory aberrations are present. We studied Bi$_2$Se$_3$ in a dipole field of a coil using a laser-based ARPES system. The electronic structure was reconstructed in post-processing using detailed electron trajectory simulations. We identify two-dimensional (2D) momentum mapping, a micron beam spot size, and precise numerical field simulations as critical technical requirements for high-resolution magneto-ARPES. We show how circular dichroism can provide additional information about the coupling of the magnetic field to the spin. The experimental achievements and the scaling laws from our simulations provide a road map towards magneto-ARPES in larger fields.
summary: This work presents a methodology to overcome severe spectral distortions in magneto-ARPES by employing detailed electron trajectory simulations. By accurately modeling how magnetic fields distort photoemitted electron paths, the authors successfully reconstruct the true electronic structure of $	ext{Bi}_2	ext{Se}_3$. This establishes critical technical guidelines for performing high-resolution ARPES measurements in strong magnetic fields.
main_problem: The primary challenge addressed is mitigating spectral distortions and broadening in magneto-ARPES measurements caused by significant electron trajectory aberrations when strong magnetic fields are applied.
main_result: The authors demonstrated that the electronic structure can be accurately reconstructed in post-processing, maintaining high momentum resolution even in the presence of strong trajectory aberrations.
method: The technique involves using detailed electron trajectory simulations (based on the equations of motion) to correct the measured photoemission angles and energies.
model_or_system: The study uses $	ext{Bi}_2	ext{Se}_3$, a topological insulator, measured using a high-resolution, laser-based ARPES system equipped with a tunable dipole magnetic field.
key_observables: Angle contraction ($	heta_f$), angle rotation ($\phi_f$), momentum distribution curves (MDCs), and the field-induced gap opening at the Dirac point.
important_parameters: The critical technical requirements identified are 2D momentum mapping, a micron beam spot size, and precise numerical field simulations. Scaling laws relating field dependence are also derived.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the electronic structure can be recovered via post-processing corrections, and residual field effects inside the analyzer lens column are neglected.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the magneto-ARPES setup, electron trajectory simulations showing contraction and rotation, and comparative plots showing the successful reconstruction of the electronic structure by applying trajectory corrections.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the technical limitations of magneto-ARPES due to trajectory aberrations, details the simulation methodology using electron equations of motion, applies this correction procedure to $	ext{Bi}_2	ext{Se}_3$ data, and finally discusses the physical implications for probing spin and orbital coupling.
why_interesting: The rigorous development of post-processing techniques to correct for complex, field-dependent electron optics effects is highly valuable for any experiment probing quantum states in external fields, bridging experimental measurement limitations with theoretical models.
